text:
Eve: Heads up — new ranker bring-up showing a divergence between two benches: anchored test set NDCG +2.1%, MRR ~0, but canary CTR down ~1.8%. Observed after PTQ->int8 pass. Anyone else seeing this pattern?
Samir: Hmm. can you paste the exact eval commands and which anchor set used? :eyes:
Eve: Sure — we ran the usual anchor_set_v3 (hand-curated) and sampled_prod_v2. Command: ```./eval_rerank --model rk-v2-ptq-int8 --anchors anchor_set_v3 --candidates 100 --seed 42 --metric ndcg,mrr```
Jin: Two quick suspects: (1) dataset mismatch (anchors are more heady), (2) priming/slot ordering differences between offline harness and prod sampler. Also kv-cache seasoning with int8 can shift ties.
Priya: Also check tokenizer parity — are we using the same tokenizer binary for the canary? We had a past bug where whitespace normalization differed between eval and prod.
Samir: Re-ran short job against the sampled_prod_v2 with the exact same binary + seed. Results: ndcg unchanged, mrr unchanged, but top1 churn shows different candidate ranking distribution (more swaps at top-3). Logged output: ```swap_rate_top3: 0.072 -> 0.095 (baseline->int8)```
Eve: Swap rate makes sense for CTR dip. Do we know if the candidate pipeline does any non-deterministic shuffling or summary truncation?
Jin: Candidate ordering pipeline has a stability flag. Canary config sets stability=false to favor freshness; offline eval had stability=true. That's a likely mismatch.
Priya: Actionable: 1) re-eval int8 model with stability=true against sampled_prod_v2 to isolate ordering. 2) run fp16 baseline with same seed and stability=false to isolate quantization delta. I can kick off (1) now.
OpsBot: Canary 2026-03-23T14:12:42Z deployed rk-v2-int8 to shard-3 (50% traffic). Health: healthy, but CTR trend observed.
Samir: I'll also dump tokenization checksums and candidate pipeline config for both eval and prod. ```sha256 tokenizer.bin -> a3f9...```
Eve: If ordering explains it, we should update the bring-up checklist: require ordering parity and tokenization checksum match before canary. If not, next suspect is calibration/rescale on logits after quantization.
Jin: For calibration probe, we should run per-layer bias-correction (our dynquant step) and compare softmax temperature shifts. Small snippet I used: ```python
# compute temp shift
logits_fp = load_logits('fp16')
logits_q = load_logits('int8')
print((logits_fp.mean(0)-logits_q.mean(0)).mean())
```
Priya: Kicking off eval now: job 4387654333 (stability=true, seed=42). Will post summary.
Samir: Posted candidate pipeline diff to PR #1429 — there's a small change in tie-handling that could increase swaps when combined with quant rounding.
Eve: Great. If anyone sees the same pattern cross-datasets (anchors vs sampled) we should also run an anchored holdout with sampled seeding (i.e., keep same candidate order but swap the labels). That isolates label vs ordering effects.
Priya: Quick update: job 4387654333 finished. Key numbers vs fp16-baseline: sampled_prod_v2 | NDCG: -0.1% | MRR: -0.05% | top1_swap_rate: 0.073 -> 0.089. So small metric deltas but swap rate persists.
Eve: Ok so ordering + quant rounding look correlated. Next steps: Samir to revert the tie-handling change in a canary build, Jin to add a small post-quant calibration pass to rescale logits, Priya to run another canary with stability=true + reverted tie-handling. I'll block full roll until we see CTR recover or we have a clear mitigation.
Samir: Assigned. I'll target a quick revert patch and a smoke canary by EOD.
Jin: I'll prototype a temp-rescale step and run a 1k example probe.
Eve: Thanks team — update thread with PR numbers and final canary CTR when available. Closing loop once we have repro around ordering+quant. :thumbsup:
